I am just taking in the fresh air in the backyard. \\nseeker: That is awesome.\\nsupporter: Thanks! What is going on in your neck of the woods? \\nseeker: Sort of stuck inside trying to make a dime but it is alright.\\nsupporter: Yeah great minds think alike.. do you do anything else for work? \\nseeker: Looking for a good job right now.\\nseeker: I wanted to talk about a personal issue I have been having, though.\\nsupporter: Okay, you know I'm here for you. Talk to me, what's happening? \\nseeker: My father and I had a fight 2 years ago and haven't spoke since.\\nsupporter: The same happened to me, and then my father passed away. If there is anything I can say, is to swallow pride and cherish the moments you have on earth together. What was the fight over?\\nseeker: Yeah I am afraid that these things can happen. It was only over material things.\\nsupporter: That was my next question, what the fight was over. Do you think he would be open to mending things? \\nseeker: It is weird because I called him out for being manipulative so this is his defense. \\nsupporter: Usually when people feel singled out, they only have a few mechanisms. Unfortunately, most people tend to run away instead of fixing things. It tends to be the easier option. \\nseeker: I would likely take advantage of an opportunity to be the bigger person.\\nsupporter: When you try to fix things, just remember that this is his method. I wouldn't hold back on what you have to say, but just word it so that he doesn't feel the need to flee. \\nseeker: That is probably decent advice.\\nsupporter: It is HIS responsibility as a parent to want to fix things, but you are also being the bigger person here. I applaud you and hope that he is receptive. \\nseeker: I hope so too, but the opportunity seems tenuous \\nsupporter: How did you guys leave it? \\nseeker: Threatening and disparagement haha\\nsupporter: Ha, well after two years, feelings had to have changed. How do you feel about it all?\\nseeker: I feel lost, to be honest. The financial pressures were already hard on us, and now without my income, I don’t know how we’ll manage.\\nsupporter: That’s a lot to handle, especially after everything you’ve been dealing with recently. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed.\\nseeker: Yeah, and I’m worried about telling Margaret. She’s just started feeling stable with her new job, and I don’t want to add more stress.\\nsupporter: It's commendable that you’re thinking about her feelings, but you're in this together. Sometimes sharing burdens can make them a bit easier to bear.\\nseeker: That's true. I just hate the idea of disappointing her or my daughter Emily. They rely on me so much.\\nsupporter: It sounds like you feel a deep sense of responsibility for your family. And it’s okay to feel that way, but remember you’re human too.\\nseeker: I know. I've been telling myself I have to be the strong one ever since Emily was in the hospital. Every issue seems bigger now.\\nsupporter: You've been strong through a lot of stressful situations, Charles. Taking care of yourself is also a part of being strong for your family.\\nseeker: You're right. I haven't really been taking the time to address how I'm feeling. I've just been pushing it aside.\\nsupporter: Would it help to talk about what lies ahead? Maybe work through some practical steps or support you might need?\\nseeker: That might help. I guess the first step is talking to Margaret, although I feel so anxious.\\nsupporter: It's natural to feel anxious, but you have a strong partnership. She might have solutions or support to offer, and being open can strengthen your relationship.\\nseeker: She’s been my rock through all of this. I do trust her, and I need to remember that.\\nsupporter: Trust is so important, and it seems like you’ve both navigated many challenges together before. Remember, you’re not alone in this.\\nseeker: Thank you for the reminder. Even when things feel heavy, it’s good to know I have people I can turn to.\\nsupporter: Always, Charles. Reaching out today was a brave step, and I hope it’s provided some clarity or solace.\\nseeker: It has, more than I expected. I’ll try to take things one day at a time and lean on my support system when I need to.\\nsupporter: Absolutely.
